terms.shortDefinition: Pay-Per-Click. The seller pays each time a shopper clicks the ad.
terms.longDefinition: Amazon PPC is the Sponsored Products, Sponsored Brands, and Sponsored Display advertising system. The seller only pays when a shopper clicks the ad, not when it is shown. A PPC VA runs that system on a client's behalf, safely.

terms.shortDefinition: Advertising Cost of Sales. Ad spend divided by ad sales.
terms.longDefinition: ACoS is the percentage of every peso of ad sales that went back to ad spend. Lower is usually better, but a planned launch may accept a higher ACoS in exchange for evidence. ACoS alone never tells you whether the campaign is failing.

terms.shortDefinition: Total Advertising Cost of Sales. Ad spend divided by total store sales.
terms.longDefinition: TACoS measures ad spend against the entire store's sales, not just sales from the ad. A falling TACoS while ACoS is flat usually means the ads are pulling in organic sales too.

terms.shortDefinition: Return on Ad Spend. Ad sales divided by ad spend.
terms.longDefinition: ROAS is the inverse of ACoS. A 4 ROAS means every peso of ad spend returned four pesos of ad sales. Both metrics tell the same story in opposite directions.

terms.shortDefinition: Cost Per Click. Ad spend divided by clicks.
terms.longDefinition: CPC is what the advertiser actually pays. A higher CPC for a converting keyword is often worth it; a high CPC on a non-converting keyword is wasted spend.

terms.shortDefinition: Click-Through Rate. Clicks divided by impressions.
terms.longDefinition: CTR measures how often shoppers who saw the ad clicked it. A low CTR usually means the listing image or title does not match what the shopper searched for.
Conversion rate tells you what percentage of clicks became orders. A high CPC with a low conversion rate is a sign the listing page is the real problem, not the campaign.
